history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed (Buddhist monastery, Nyingma sect). Built in the iron-dog year of the 14th Rabjung cycle, corresponding to 1850 AD, per the Sikkim Ecclesiastical Department (sikkimeccl.gov.in); Wikipedia's Lachung Monastery article instead gives 1880 as the establishment year — conflict flagged, (verify). The site previously belonged to Bon worshippers and was converted into a Buddhist monastery by locals to strengthen Buddhist faith in the region. In 1930 statues of Buddha, Guru Padmasambhava and Chenrezig (copper) plus Kangyur and Tengyur texts were brought from Tibet as the gompa's basic religious treasure; renovated and remodeled by the lamas in 1983. Hosts an annual mask dance in winter. Coordinates used are the monastery coordinates from Wikipedia's Lachung Monastery article (27.6167, 88.65). CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name 'Lachung' — corrected to Sikkim.

name: Samten Choling Monastery
town_description: Lachung is a mountain village in North Sikkim at about 3,000 m, at the confluence of the Lachen and Lachung rivers. A former Indo-Tibet trading post and the last village before the Indo-China border, it is the gateway to the Yumthang Valley; permits are required for visits to North Sikkim.

travel.airport: Nearest airport: Bagdogra (IXB), Siliguri. Also Pakyong Airport (flights infrequent).
travel.road: 118 km from Gangtok via the North Sikkim Highway; reachable by hired taxi or shared jeep. Protected Area Permit required for North Sikkim.

visitor_information.best_time: October–May (Lachung is cut off in peak monsoon and winter; confirm road status before travel).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify); monasteries in the region are generally open dawn–dusk.
